correctness.rationale: The product of the positive denominators is positive for all real P and monic of degree 2m (the empty product is 1). Clearing it leaves a polynomial of degree 2m+1 with leading coefficient -a: all recycling contributions have degree at most 2m. Multiplicity of a root is preserved because its denominator is nonzero. An attracting isolated positive root must have positive field immediately to its left and negative immediately to its right, since otherwise a solution on that side cannot approach it; thus any two attracting roots enclose a different root. This includes nonhyperbolic roots. For simultaneous sharpness start at m=0 with the two witnesses 0 and 1. Adding (K,3K) contributes at each old witness at most 3P^2/K, so all prior strict signs persist for sufficiently large K. At the new witness K the field is at least L+K/2; at 4K it is below L+sum(old r)-K, made negative by the same large-K choice. These are ordered after the last prior witness and add two sign changes. The resulting distinct positive roots saturate the degree bound and must all be simple, with alternating stability. The argument uses finite K at every fixed stage and proves all-m attainability, not a numerical cutoff. Independently evaluated the six stated two-channel witnesses with integer-safe rational substitution: 1/10, -906517/32500520, 9499/100040, -13/626, 7199/117290, -50783079899/252501010. Positive loading keeps the half-line forward invariant and the linear-loss upper bound gives global boundedness. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The sign-based stability count is for the deterministic scalar ODE. Time delays, additional dynamic states, spatial feedbacks, and field parameter constraints are not part of the claim.

value.rationale: An exact simultaneous upper bound and realization settle whether a fixed shallow Hill nonlinearity intrinsically caps the number of stable scalar regimes independently of how many feedback pathways are included. The construction answers no without replacing the nonlinearities by step functions, using negative feedback gains, or adding state variables. This is a structural distinction between a one-channel textbook example and the unbounded number of regimes attainable with finite positive channels.
residual_risks: The wide separation of scales may be unphysical; the theorem does not support a prediction of actual lake regimes or a management intervention.
